To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

manure processing technologies that separate manure into a liquid and solid fraction and de-water the liquid fraction by reverse osmosis, can reduce the environmental impact of animal manure in terms of global warming and fossil fuel depletion when bio-energy is produced, and can reduce eutrophication and acidification when ammonia emissions are low.

processing of pig and dairy cattle liquid manure into a liquid mineral fertilizer and a solid manure fraction for bio-energy production increases the environmental impact in most impact categories, except climate change for dairy cattle manures.
manure processing to produce fertilizer and bio-energy increases environmental impact compared to current manure handling, unless bio-energy production is combined with anaerobic digestion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the environmental consequences of manur processing technologies that are currently being developed and applied.
a novel manure processing technology, the so-called manure processing technology (MPT).
the development and implementation of sustainable animal manure management systems that are economically viable and that contribute to the reduction of environmental problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the processing of pig and cattle manure to mineral fertilizer and bio-fertilizer has an environmental impact on climate change, acidification and eutrophization, particulate matter formation, and fossil fuel depletion, and that the production of bio-fuel can reduce this environmental impact.
the environmental performance of manure processing depends on the manure type, the processing method and the use of the end products.

processing manure to separate the solid and liquid fraction followed by anaerobic digestion and subsequent bio-energy production is a promising technology for manure management, especially for dairy cattle manures, to address environmental problems such as global warming, acid rain, eutrophication, and fossil fuel depletion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the environmental impact of processing liquid manure to produce fertilizer and bio-energy can be reduced when manure processing technologies are improved, and bio-energy is produced.
manure processing is not a sustainable solution for all manure management problems.
the environmental consequences of manuring with processed manure can be reduced by including anaerobic digestion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
manure processing technologies are not a one-size-fits-all solution.
the processing technology has the potential to improve the overall environmental performance of manure management, but only when NH3 emission is minimized.
processing manure to mineral fertilizer and bio-gas can be environmentally advantageous, but only under specific conditions.
